utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good morning, Doctor.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: This morning Ms. Kravetz has some questions for you. Ms. Kravetz.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Good morning, Dr. Stankovic.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Sir, I want to take you back to portions of your report and your testimony that you gave yesterday, and I want to start with page 2 of your report which refers to P1167, the report of the Austrian team regarding the Kotlina site.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And I would ask that that be put up on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And just so you know, sir, we're going to go through your report, but not necessarily in the same order you discussed it yesterday with my learned colleague. So I'll just let you know which specific pages of your report I'm referring to as I move along. So in relation to P1167, the Austrian report, you made a series of comments yesterday, and I would like to direct your attention to paragraph 2 of your -- of page 2 of your report. I believe it's the same in the English. And these are comments in relation to body number 4. Are you there, sir, with me, body number 4?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Now, in relation to this the description contained in the Austrian report, the Swiss Austrian report, in relation to body number 4, you made a comment that there was first a claim that there was -- the body showed signs of injury by fire-arm, but then the report stated that it was caused by shrapnel and you found this to be an inconsistent finding. Do you remember saying that, sir? That's your position regarding this, sir; is that a correct understanding?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Now I would like to take you to page 5 in the English of the report and it's also page 5 in the B/C/S. And this is a preliminary section of the report where the team that participated in the exhumations and in evidence collection is indicated. And we see here, sir, if we he look at this table that it says evidence recorded by crime scene group Austria and a certain three persons there are listed. And then we see autopsies conducted by, and we have Mr. Markwalder, about whom you spoke yesterday, and then Daniel Wyler. Do you see that, sir, that we have these indications of two different teams, one who was at the scene recording the evidence and the other one that conducted the autopsies; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Now, if we move to page 12 in the English and also page 12 in the B/C/S, and this is the section that referred to body number 4, if we could have that up on the screen -- and, sir, I presume you know from having read the report that the evidence collection at the site took place between the 7th and 9th of September, whereas the autopsies took place in Kacanik cemetery and that was done starting on the 13th of September. You are aware of that, no, from having reviewed the report?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, certainly.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Now, if we look at page 12 we have body number 4, and we see that it's talking about the exhumation of the body, and in the information referring to the exhumation it talks about a hole presumably a bullet wound was visible in the torso on the back and to the right of the spinal column. Now, if we go to the next page, this is page 13 both in the English and the B/C/S, we see the comments made by Dr. Markwalder who conducted the autopsy on the 13th of September, that is some days after this body was exhumed. And in his comments he says: "The body was practically complete as far as the region of the head. Marks of an explosion and fire were present on the corpse, and superficial skin lesions were visible on the back, possibly splinter wounds." Now, sir, isn't a reasonable reading of this description, this section of body number 4, that, in fact, the comments right under the name and which refer to the exhumation were comments made by the persons who were at the scene and collected the evidence, and Dr. Markwalder's comments when he performed the autopsy are actually only those on page 13 of the report? Isn't that a reasonable reading based on the way these -- the exhumations and the autopsies were performed?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not in my view. If we were to analyse a process of exhumation, then on the site there must be a forensic medical expert, a forensic pathologist --

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- who needs to register --

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: I'm sorry to interrupt you, but we're speaking specifically of the methodology used by this team, and what I'm asking is based on the methodology that is indicated in the report, wouldn't a reasonable reading of this entry referring to body number 4 be that, in fact, both these comments cannot be attributed to Dr. Markwalder because this section that refers to him is only the section on page 13 which refers to the body showing marks of an explosion? That is, in fact, the section with his comments, no, sir? Isn't that a reasonable reading on -- based on what we know of the methodology used by this team that was on site?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Within a team everyone has his or her responsibilities, which they need to meet, as permitted by their professional background. Therefore, no one is to interpret what is outside his or her competence. Those who were in charge of the exhumations when they realised there had been a wound, they should have said a wound in the region of the back, and they should not have gone into what the weapon may have been. In this specific case one gets the impression that within the same team working on the same task there was no co-ordination. It's rather as if everyone was working something they deemed necessary, which is not a permissible principle when there is team-work involved.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: I understand that that is your position. All I'm asking is: Isn't it correct from reading the report that the comments made by Dr. Markwalder are only those that appear on page 13? Isn't that what the report says? And I understand your position on this.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After the examination he stated what is in the report, as you quoted it. On the scene they -- well, he must have checked what had been written by the experts who were present at the site when the exhumation was carried out. In that case, at least in the remarks to his autopsy findings, he should have specified the discrepancy between what was stated on the scene during the exhumation and the conclusion he reached when examining the mortal remains.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Yes, and that goes outside -- or beyond the scope of what I was asking. I understand that is your criticism or complaint regarding this specific injury. Now, if we move on in your report, paragraph 3 and 4, you refer to the fact that no traces of projectiles were found in the trees around the upper and lower well and the fact that soot-covered fragments of fabric were found in the vicinity of the well as factors that indicate that the bodies were brought from elsewhere and thrown into the well. Correct, that is your position that these are indications that the bodies were brought from elsewhere?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Among other pieces of information which indicate that there were no executions on that site, that these two pieces of information certainly make part of that body of information as a whole.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Now, in relation to paragraph 4, yesterday you said - and this is the paragraph referring to the soot-covered fragments fabric - you said: "In the process of the bodies being moved, given that there were traces of flame visible on the bodies, the clothing particles referred to fell off the bodies and some of them ended up close to the well shaft." This is transcript 13415. Sir, you don't really have any information, do you, of how it is that fragments of clothing made it -- or were found outside the well, you don't know how that got there, no?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In any case, having in mind the depth of the well --

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- they could not have --

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: I'm just asking -- I'm going to ask you -- I'm sorry I'm interrupting you but since we have a lot of material to get through today, just to focus on my questions. Do you have any specific information to affirm that the clothing of -- fragments of clothing that were found outside the well actually fell off the bodies as they were being carried to the well? Do you have information to affirm that? I mean, any personal knowledge to affirm that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have any personal knowledge, but as I said yesterday, if certain body parts were burned in the location where the charred pieces of fabric were found, then in addition to those pieces of fabric one would have expected to find parts of the human body. If such parts or pieces are missing, then it is highly likely that as the bodies were being carried the charred items or pieces of fabric simply fell off and landed on the location where they were found.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And when you say that it's highly likely that the bodies -- that as the bodies were being carried, charred items or pieces of fabric fell off, this is actually just a guess from your part, isn't it, sir? I mean, you -- you're not really in a position to affirm that that is what happened and that is how those pieces of fragment made it there, no?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Based on the description of the place where those traces were found, I arrived at the conclusion that they ended up there when the corpses were carried. For, there was no other way for them to be there. The only other possibility was that someone intentionally collected them elsewhere and then have those strewn around the places where the bodies were found.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: So there are different possibilities, sir, no? And you are just giving us one -- what could be one possibility. There are many different possibilities of what happened and how these fragments made it there, no, sir?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I have said, there are two possibilities: Either that those items of fabric ended up there when the bodies were carried or that someone intentionally spread them around the area. There's no other possibility. Having in mind the depth of the well, it would have been impossible for those pieces to fly out of the well shaft from the depth of 8 to 9 metres, as was registered.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Sir, if we look at page 7 of the report --

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: If we could have that up on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And this is a description of the crime scene. Could we have -- yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Could we also have it up on the screen in English, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Now, we see here, sir, that what the report actually says is that there were a few soot-covered fragments of fabric in the vicinity of the crime scene. Do you see that it says that, sir, that it refers to a few soot-covered fragments of fabric?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And if we go to the next page, and this is page 8, and this refers to the collection of evidence and recovery of bodies, and it's also a description of the crime scene, we he see that in relation to both of the wells, the upper and the lower well, the report indicates that the wall -- the walls of the well shaft, that is, inside the well, was blackened with soot. Do you see that, sir, that both for the upper and the lower well that's indicated?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And we see also that a soil test was carried out in the blackened area of the well and the report -- we see that later on in the report, I'm not going to go to the page, but it's on page 91 and 117 -- 91 of the English and 117 of the B/C/S, it shows -- the report also says that tests were conducted on this sample and, in fact, the tests showed that this soil sample contained signs of TNT. Do you recall reading that, that the tests conducted in the soil sample taken from inside the well showed that it had signs of TNT, of explosives inside? Do you recall reading that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And the report also tells us - and you can access that in many places, but a summary of it is on page 72 of the English and 98 of the B/C/S - it tells us that: "Exhumation from the upper well resulted in a total of seven bodies which were severely damaged from the effects of the explosion of fire, and of the lower well the exhumation resulted in a finding of 15 bodies which were also severely damaged from the effects of the explosions." Do you recall reading that in the report, sir? And these specific descriptions of the damages are also in the individual entries that referred to each body. I imagine you read through that when you were reviewing this report?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You probably listened to what I said yesterday. I did not deny the existence of blast injuries.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: So, sir, we have this expert team finding marks of soot inside the well, samples taken, and signs of explosives are found from the soil inside the well, the bodies that are found inside the well all showed signs of being severely damaged by effects of explosives. And you are telling us that based on what is in your report, these are not bodies that were blown up inside the well, but they were, in fact, brought from elsewhere? Is that what you are saying, sir, despite these findings that are made in the report?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is my conclusion.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Very well, sir. One of the points that you make is -- and again, to indicate that these bodies were not killed at the site, and this is at page -- in paragraph 6 of your report - relates to the number of cartridges found at the well. And you make the point that there are only 12 spent shells found and that the bodies examined indicate that there were at least 26 gun-shot wounds. And I believe you also indicated yesterday that given that the bodies had signs of explosions there could have been more gun-shot wounds in the parts that were actually not found, the body -- the parts that were blown up by the explosion. Do you recall saying that, that you believe the number of gun-shot wounds was higher than the number of spent shell casings found there? And this was one of your -- the points you made to indicate that the killings did not occur inside. Is that a correct understanding of your evidence?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I said that the number of the spent cartridges found does not reflect the number of wounds. There were far fewer of them than there were registered gun-shot wounds on the bodies.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And your conclusion to say that the bodies were not killed on site is in this case simply or merely based on the absence of the number of shell casings?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. If you followed closely what I said about the location in Kotlina --

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- there are 21 items --

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: -- I'm speaking specifically about paragraph 6. What you're saying in paragraph 6 is this is an element -- the absence of shell casings is an element to say the bodies were not killed in the well? That's what you're basing your conclusion on; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is only one element of my conclusion. There are other elements indicating that those people were not shot there but elsewhere.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: You would agree with me, sir, that there's several other alternative explanations for the absence of shell casings at the site, no?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We don't have any other explanations in the material I reviewed.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: But you do know, sir, that a period of approximately six months had passed between the -- when these alleged killings took place and when this examination took place, this happened -- the examinations or the exhumations and forensic examinations took place in September; right? So this -- a long period of time had passed from the alleged killings; you would agree with me on that, no?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was a certain period of time between the time of death and the finding.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And we don't really know what happened to those shell casings. For all we know someone could have gone to the site, picked them up -- we really don't know, do we, sir? We don't have information of what could have happened in that period of almost six months to explain the absence of shell casings?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there were so many spent shells in the whole of Kosovo, and I don't know how is one to interpret all that, if one needs to go up a slope which is at an angle of 50 degrees and whether one needs to go up that slope only to collect spent casings, I'm not really sure.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: But you would agree with me, sir, that there are different possibilities of what could have happened there, no? We really can't say what happened based on the information we have?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if someone had intentionally collected the spent cartridges, then there is that possibility, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Now, sir, moving on in your report, paragraph 7, you speak about the fact that dismembered body parts were found in different layers of the well, that they were found in the top layer, they were found in the bottom lawyer. And you reached the conclusion that the body parts were brought and they were thrown into the well. Are you suggesting, sir, that someone went around, collected fragments of -- small fragments of body parts and then threw them into these well shafts? Is that what you're suggesting is your interpretation of the finding made by the Swiss/Austrian team?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Based on the position of the bodies, it would appear so. It appears that someone gathered those mortal remains and threw them down the well.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: You don't have information of how these explosions happened, do you, sir?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And do you allow for the possibility that there were multiple explosions at different times? That is a possibility, sir, isn't it, a group of bodies is thrown in, grenades are thrown, then another group of bodies is thrown down the well. That is a possibility, isn't it, sir?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is that possibility; however, the number of metal fragments found in the well does not confirm this assumption since, as you yourself know, a small number was found, I think 16. Just one moment, please. I think only 16 metal fragments were found in the well area. If several bombs were thrown, then it would be a realistic thing to expect to find a larger number of metal fragments in the well than the ones that were actually found.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: So you're basing your conclusion solely on the fact of the metal -- the number of metal fragments found in the well?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I already told you that my findings indicate the conclusion that I referred to, not -- the conclusion is not based on one segment of it. I analysed each of the possibilities. I collated and analysed the facts through a large number of examples, which I explained, and on the basis of all of that evidence, I drew the conclusion that I talked about yesterday. This again is just one of the conclusions that would indicate that the bodies were not killed in the well but at some other location.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Well, let's look at another one of your conclusions, and this is paragraph 8. In paragraph 8 you referred to three bodies; body 5, body 12, and body 13. And you indicate that these are bodies that are found either on the stomach or on their front. And you say: "If injuries inflicted by an explosive device had occurred, the wounds would be located on the back, that is, on the back part of the body in which the explosion mine or explosive fell." Now, sir, what the report is telling us is the position in which the bodies were found at the time of the exhumation; correct? That is what the report is telling us?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And we do not know based on the information we have which was the position the bodies were in the well shaft at the time the explosions occurred; correct? We don't have that information?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We don't have that information.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Now, sir, you've picked three examples from this report of bodies found on their front, but there are a total of 22 bodies that were found in these two well shafts. And if we go through -- I'm not going to go through each one of them, but we do have examples of, for example, body 15 and 22, which are bodies that were torn to shreds by the effects of the explosions or bodies 1, 16, 18, which had extremities or the head missing as a result of the explosions and other bodies that showed signs of explosions or in other parts, not only on the stomach. Now, sir, this criticism that you make in paragraph 8 and your conclusion that these bodies -- this shows that the bodies were brought from elsewhere, in fact, is a valid conclusion with respect to all the bodies that are found in these two wells, is it, sir?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I picked characteristic cases which point to the distribution of the blast injuries which could not have been caused in the well in the event explosive device was thrown into the well. At the same time, I said that the bodies that I referred to and that you also referred to for the most part - and this is in paragraph 9 of my report - have that extent of destruction which would indicate that it was impossible that it was caused in the well because only 16 fragments of metal were found in the well. So the 16 metal fragments found in the well would not really lead to the conclusion or indicate that the injuries were caused in the well.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Yes, and you have already told us that. But, sir, doesn't the position in which the body was at the time of the explosion determine where the explosion injuries would appear on the body or where there would be? Isn't this the factor that determines which part of the body is affected by the explosions, the actual position they were in at the time when the explosions took place?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And for all we know, sir, I mean, we don't know what -- you don't know what type of explosives were thrown in, do you, sir, what type of explosives were used in this case?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From what you've said it's certain that explosive devices were not thrown in in the way it is stated, hand-grenades or any other kind of explosive devices were not thrown in.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Sir, but you don't know what sort of explosives were used here? You don't have that information?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't. You said that in the analysis TNT was found in the walls of the well. You said that a little bit earlier. I don't have the whole report, I only have segments of it so I really cannot comment on that, but what I am saying is that with the destruction of this extent we don't have any body parts found on the walls of the well, which would be a logical thing if we have in mind the nature of an explosion and having in mind the fact that the body's made up of soft tissue and bone, which in that case would be imprinted on the or impacted on the walls of the well. An explosive device would throw the bodies to the side, and had a blast occurred in the well it would be realistic then to expect that the earth and walls of the well would also contain bone fragments which would have struck the walls of the well. We don't have such findings, and we cannot really claim or make any assertions about things for which we have no material evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Yes, that is, in fact, my point, sir, that we don't have elements to make the conclusions in fact that you're making, that these bodies were brought from elsewhere because we would need to know, for example, what sort of explosives were used, the position of the bodies at the time of the explosions, no? These are information we would need to know to reach the conclusions that you're reaching?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, but you are the Prosecutor. When do you have a situation in a crime, let's say an explosion as a result of a terrorist act, where you do have information about the positions of the body before the explosion? And when somebody gives you information, for example, the blast occurred in a subway, for example, the bodies of the people were turned with their backs to the blast and that is why the injuries occurred to the back. Again, I am saying the bodies were on their stomachs at the time death occurred or at the time when the bodies were thrown in the well. If somebody had thrown in a mine or an explosive device, it would be normal for the injury to occur on the back. Why would this be on the stomach? I don't know. I have no explanation for that. Perhaps someone else does, and I would like to hear that from them, and in that case we could talk about it and discuss it and see.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: But, sir, for all me know hand-grenades were thrown in the well all the way down to the well and the explosions happened there and that's where those bodies were that suffered injuries on their stomach, no? That could be a possibility of what happened? I mean, there are many possibilities, sir, no? Isn't that correct, to explain that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said -- no, what you just said is not possible in view of the number of the metal fragments that were found in the well area with a device such as a metal detector. Such a small number of metal fragments, a small number of explosive devices thrown cannot inflict such destructive injuries that I referred to in paragraph 9 of my findings. You're talking about witnesses. We had yesterday a witness here who claimed that --

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Sir, I think you're going outside the scope of my question, so I'm going to stop you so we can move on. Now, one of the comments you made with regard to this report yesterday is that you were surprised by the short descriptions contained in the section on the autopsies, the description made by Markwalder, no, that they were very cursory comments on the state of the bodies? That is one of your complaints, isn't it, sir?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Now, sir, in your report don't you also make, in fact, very cursory observations with regard to each one of these bodies when you're reaching your conclusions? Isn't that something you do in your own report? You don't provide any analysis, do you, sir, on the different points that you make in your report?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was told that my report would need to contain very short assertions. I'm not here for the first time. I'm appearing before this Tribunal for the fourth and fifth time. So when my analysis was very broad I was told that in a trial like this details will be explained, just as I did that yesterday. We went through the information with the Defence lawyer. So now I'm explaining my conclusions, my assertions, as a person who has done this kind of expertise before. I had before me the data that we're talking about. My task was for each one of these cases I was supposed to write a broader explanation than what is described as an autopsy here. Then we would have material that would number a couple of thousand of pages. It's something that I can write very quickly if necessary, but I believe that I acted pursuant to the instructions I received, and that is why the report is in this form.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Okay. Very well, sir. Now, we see from the comments made, and I want to show you one example, and this is on page 18, it's body number 8. And the autopsy comments are actually on page 19. And this is a body where Dr. Markwalder says: "Explosion and fire marks were found on the body. Most of the body was missing. Only remains of the legs, both feet and various remnants of clothing could be accounted for. No entry wounds were found." Now, you've said that you were a bit surprised by the short descriptions that Dr. Markwalder made in his report, but here we have a case, sir, where the head is missing. And he can't really do anything about the head and the fact that parts of the body are missing, can he, sir? I mean, this is as much of a description as he can give based on the state of this specific body that was found? Would you agree with me on that, sir?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't see where it says that the head is missing. Where does it say in the report that the head is missing?

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Well, I'm sorry, it says most of the body's missing. So, in fact, he had very little of the body to examine in this case, not only no head but it says both legs -- all that remained were legs and feet. I mean, there's not much more he can say, can he, if this is the condition of the remains of body number 8 that he's examining, can he, sir?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Unfortunately he could have done much more. I don't want to dispute Markwalder's work now or in any way question his professional integrity, but if you are working in conditions - I mentioned that yesterday - that are peaceful, when there are no combat action, when you have the technical equipment, when you have the necessary means, you can really say much more in this particular part. The autopsy report must be much more precise. You need to explain if there is no head. You have the sections in the autopsy report which are external findings, internal findings, the head, neck, and the chest, the stomach and the extremities. And you have to describe what is there and what is missing of these body parts. It's not stated here, so I am surprised. I did remark on that. I would like you to see the protocols that I provided to the Tribunal, to the Prosecutor's office, and I worked in the midst of combat at the time when there was still combat. So the only person who actually worked in a combat-affected area was me. So I don't understand how people who are engaged by an institution like this, such as the Hague Tribunal, and in cases where Prosecutors of this level are working. I really have a lot of respect for you and all the questions, and now you're being put in a position that because of somebody else's superficial work you are putting 10, 20, 30 questions to me. You're trying to confirm your indictment, whereas the person who was supposed to have --

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Sir, I'm sorry, I'm going to stop you there. You're going well beyond the scope of my question, sir, and making comments that do not relate at all --

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's possible that I did go beyond the scope. I apologise if you tell me I have three seconds, I will say what I can in three seconds. I mean, there's no problem about that. But you just tell me the rule. Sometimes when I am very brief then -- all right.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Let's just go back to me asking questions, and I'll just ask you to focus on the questions I'm asking. And you've given us your point on the fact that I was raising. Sir, if we can move on in your report, paragraph 12, you say in paragraph 12: "The penetrating and blast injuries found on different body parts indicate that the injuries most probably occurred during an armed clash between two sides to the conflict." And you said yesterday in relation to this, you say: "My experience in finding in one body various injuries which were inflicted with different objects such as gun-shot wounds and injuries from mines and explosives, then that indicates that such injuries could have been inflicted and most likely were inflicted during armed conflict between warring sides." That's at transcript page 13421. Now, sir, you don't really have sufficient information to state that, do you, about the specific site?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I drew the conclusion on the basis of 5.000 autopsies that I conducted in a combat-affected area. If I do not have the right on the basis of that number of autopsies to have my opinion and to make conclusions, then that is quite a different matter.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: What I'm asking, sir, is specific to this site, you do not know the specific circumstances in which these killings occurred, so you don't actually have sufficient information with regard to this specific site of how -- whether these persons were killed in an armed clash or in any other manner? You don't know that, sir, do you?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but I wrote "most probably," not "certainly," but most probably or most likely which means that there is a slight possibility for a different option. Had I said I was sure -- had I been sure, I would have said I was sure.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Okay. So there are other options is what I understand you're saying. Now, sir, if we move to paragraph 15 you referred to the injuries sustained by body number 20. And you say: "The described injury to the left side of the neck an injury caused by a sharp instrument, knife wound, as stated in the autopsy report, body 20, page 32, could also have been caused by pieces of shrapnel taking into account the movement of shrapnel and the degree and depth of damage of soft tissue on the neck." And in relation to this yesterday you said: "Therefore, given the appearance and the description of this wound, I believe the most -- that most likely this injury was also caused by one of the shrapnels because if somebody had wanted to torture this victim they wouldn't have stopped at just one knife stab. This is the experience I have after having performed all those autopsies. So they wouldn't have stopped at just one knife stab that didn't damage any arteries. It is just unlikely." This is at 13424. Now, sir, again, you do not know how this injury was caused, do you?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again I stated my view on it with a certain degree of certainty. What is in the text that you have just read out, that investigation has found that this wound did not cause damage to any vital arteries, indicating that it was a superficial injury of the soft tissue of the skin and possibly subcutaneous tissue. So I don't see any purpose of anyone inflicting such superficial wounds with a knife without wishing to do something worse or to cause worse damage than what is described here.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: So you're saying you don't see any purpose of anyone inflicting such superficial wounds if they hadn't wanted to stab this person further; is that what you're saying, that if this was a knife wound, the person who caused it would probably have wanted to stab this victim several times? Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am saying that on the basis of the description and the way the injury looked, you cannot with full certainty state that it was inflicted by a knife. In my view, since a number of shrapnel wounds on the back were also seen, it's most likely that this injury was caused in this way. This is what I said.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: But you don't know anything, sir, about what was the intention of the person who may have inflicted this knife wound, do you? You don't know that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know, and I'm not talking about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And you didn't examine the body yourself?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And you would agree that those persons examining the body would be best placed to determine whether this was a knife wound or not? You would agree with me based on your experience of the thousands of autopsies that you've conducted?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I agree with you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Okay. Let's move on from that, sir. Now, let's look at paragraph 19, where you say: "The autopsies of the bodies did not find injuries indicating that people were beaten up before they were thrown into the well and died, as stated by witnesses." Now, sir, if we go to body number 7, and this starts on page 15, and the conclusions are on page 16, the autopsy description indicates: "Explosions and fire marks were found on the body. No gun-shot wounds were visible on the body. The skull was broken by the force of a dull blow." Now, sir, I put to you that isn't this at least one example of an injury that would correspond to the eye-witness report that these persons were beaten?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said at the same time that the bone fractures and the skull fracture could have been caused when the bodily remains were thrown into the well and with the impact of those parts of the body on hard surfaces or other bodies. So if somebody did perform an autopsy, they could have referred to all of the possibilities, and that is my objection because the person who did the autopsy did not explain the mechanism of the inflicting of each of the wounds. It's just a general theory that it could be perhaps the head striking a blunt object, and that is how the injury could have been caused.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And when you say that this injury could have been caused by the body falling into the well and the impact with other bodies, you're, in fact, just making an assumption there, aren't you, sir, because again you don't have information to state that that's the case with respect to this body?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the same way that the assertion is made in the autopsy that the skull was crushed by a dull blow. They also don't have any grounds for such an assertion. Had they referred to all of the possibilities including the one that I mention, that it could have been caused by a fall and impact on a blunt object, then I would not have been making objections to this report. There's a kind of exclusivity here where certain things are being ruled out and only one thing is being referred to. The injury's been explained with only one possibility and not with several possibility. I took into account all the mechanisms and possible ways to inflict the injury, and I'm referring to this possibility as well. When one explains an injury, and let's say that a fracture of the skull was noted or an injury to the skull with an impacted fracture, then I could say that it could have been caused by a blunt injury or an object. It could have been a bat, a pole, a metal bar. All of these are possibilities that I would need to mention in my report, then in the course of an investigation or proceedings like this, the trial or the Chamber would on the basis of all the material evidence collected during an investigation decide on the actual cause of the injury. There is only one possibility that is being referred to here, and this is something that I could not accept.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: But, sir, just like in the case of the stab injury or knife injury we just saw, wouldn't those persons who are examining the remains of this body be the ones best placed to make a determination on what they're observing of how this injury was caused? Wouldn't they be the ones best placed? I mean, you're giving different possibilities, but you didn't examine the bodies. Wouldn't those persons who examined the bodies be in a better position than you to make an assessment as to how this injury was caused?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Prosecutor, but it was their duty, knowing that this is evidence that would be looked at in a court proceedings, to describe in detail what the injury looked like, meaning the size of it, whether it was a linear fracture, impacted fracture, if it's a line fracture then it's an injury or a skull fracture inflicted by striking a hard surface. If it's an indented fracture then it could be caused with the head sustaining the injury in a fall. So all these elements are not mentioned here. For any kind of conclusion making that is precise, you would need to refer to all the possibilities. We just have one assertion that does not necessarily arise from --

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Sir, and you've already given us your position on that, so I'm just going to interrupt you just so we don't go -- we move on and don't go over the same point again. Let me direct your attention to paragraph 20 of your report, of the same section of the report. This is on page 4. In paragraph 20 you refer to the material evidence found on site and you say: "Material evidence of a Chinese-made-calibre bullet from 1964 was found -- material evidence 1 is a Chinese-made -- is 7.62 times 3.9-millimetre calibre bullet from 1964." And then you say: "During the armed conflict and long before that the Army of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia and the police of the Republic of Serbia did not have any ammunition of its origin -- of this origin or -- and date of manufacture." Now, sir, if we turn to page 75 of the report.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: If we could have that up.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: It's the page that refers to -- and it's page 101 in the B/C/S. It refers to this Chinese -- it's 101 in B/C/S and page 75 in the English. And it's a section that refers to the material evidence found on site. I'm just waiting for that to come up, sir. I think we have the wrong page in both languages. Well, I'll -- 75 in the English, 101 in the B/C/S. While that is being brought up, sir, just so we move on, on page 75 it says that -- what was found was, in fact, one rifle cartridge with a full jacket bullet and it's of Chinese manufacture. So what was found there was one bullet of Chinese manufacture; correct? That's what it says there at the top of the page. And I'm sorry that we have the wrong page in the B/C/S up because I've asked for page 105 [sic] and I see we have page 75. That is what was found, sir, no, that you're referring to in your report is one bullet of Chinese manufacture.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, one bullet.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And doesn't the report tell us -- we can see it's on the same page that, in fact, 12 cartridge, rifle cartridge cases were found on site, and if we read page 75 and the following pages, the report indicates that these cartridge cases had, in fact, Cyrillic letters and that they were of Yugoslav munitions factory, they were produced there. You saw that in the report as well, no, that munition of Yugoslav origin was found, and it's described in page 76, and it goes on in the English and also in the B/C/S. You are aware, sir, that that was found also on site?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did not dispute that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: So this comment you make, sir, that there was one bullet of Chinese made found on site doesn't really tell us anything, does it, about what had -- about what happened there?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It does. It tells us that that bullet did not come from the members of the police and army who were in the area of Kosovo. Official units could not have had such a bullet, and this is what I said.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Okay. So that's all we can say, really, there was one bullet. It wasn't a bullet that was used by the army or the police. That's all we can say, really, but it doesn't tell us anything more about what actually happened, how that bullet got there. We don't know any of that, do we, sir?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, one can have different interpretation, but it is up -- interpretations, but it's up to the Court to decide.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Very well, sir. And if we can move to paragraph 21 of your same report of the same page. You say there: "Judging by the age of the people whose bodies were found in the well, the youngest was born in 1982, the oldest in 1944. They were capable of carrying arms and taking part in war operations." And I believe yesterday you went into -- elaborated on this a bit more and referred to the different ages that you had seen there. And you said the conclusions is that these were able-bodied persons who could discharge military duties. Sir, is it usual for you to make these type of conclusions in forensic reports that you prepare? Is it part of your forensic expertise to say whether the victims were capable of carrying arms and taking part in war operations?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We have a number of cases heard by our courts for participation in combat activities. Claims for damages are submitted by certain parties for compensation from the state. They allege that they were not competent to serve a military term because they had been ill. Based on evidence from the medical records, such allegations are discussed. In our expert opinions, we also provide such opinions as we do with people of different degrees of injuries or handicap resulting from an earlier injury or other body limitations. We need to assess what their physical abilities are. For example, if there are injuries to the fingers of the right hand, we need to assess whether that person could have fired from a weapon at the time a crime was committed --

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Sir, but we're not in a situation of a claim for damages case here, are we, sir? This is not what this is about.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which doesn't necessarily mean that it couldn't be so. The families of those killed lost the most, and even tomorrow they can sue for damages, sue those who killed these people or forced them to do something.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: So you're saying, sir, that you made this comment in the report out of interest for the families of the victims who some day in the future could sue for damages? That was the purpose behind making such a statement in your report; is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The only thing I say is that based on one's age - and this is what I addressed - is important. I did not assess their medical condition or anything else. I merely stated my opinion based on their age, whether they could carry arms and take part in combat. This is just a narrow part of the general assertion you're making. I'm not addressing their health status. They may have well been sick, but based on the autopsy findings we don't have such information.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Sir, but I asked you for your reason for -- I asked you why this was in the report, and you started speaking about the claim for damages cases. In fact, sir, aren't you just making this comment here to undermine this report and to support the Defence case regarding this incident. Isn't that the only reason why you're making such a statement in your report?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You asked me whether as part of my expert opinions I also make use of this type of information and conclusions. I was trying to explain to you what my role is as a forensic medical expert. I also included in that explanation the cases I have just explained so as to illustrate that there are situations like that. In this case, as I've said already, I only stated that based on the age of the victims they were able to serve a military term or carry out military duties.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Sir, I believe you haven't answered my question. What I'm asking you is your reason for doing that in this case. We're not dealing with a claim for damages case. Isn't the only reason you did that was just simply to undermine this report and support the Defence case regarding this specific incident; isn't that why that is in your report in this case with regard to the Kotlina incident?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Whether those people were able to carry arms, that was the only reason I had in mind when I expressed my opinion whether these people were fit for military service. I don't know what the position of Defence is and what they propose.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Very well, sir, we're going to move on in your report, and as I say, we're not going to go in the order the different reports are analysed. I'm going to jump around a bit, and I want to go to page 10 which refers to the Izbica site, and this is P1165, if we could have that up on the screen. And I'm just waiting, sir, to -- for that to come up before discussing it with you. Now, sir, you referred to this report on page 10 and you say, and I'm just drawing your attention to paragraph 1, you say that: "It is alleged that the forces of the Republic of Serbia and the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia rounded up approximately 150 people." And then you go on to say that: "84 military bullet fragments were collected," and your conclusion is: "So it follows that just over half the people suffered one penetrating wound each and that just under half of the people did not suffer any penetrating wounds." So essentially what you're saying is although there's an allegation that over a hundred people were killed here based on the military fragments -- bullet fragments found, your assessment is that less people suffered any type of penetrating wound. Is that a correct understanding of what your conclusion here is on page 1 -- on paragraph 1?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I said that based on the number of persons and based on the number of cartridges collected in the locations where it is alleged that they were killed, one comes to realise that there is a difference between the number of cartridges found and the number of gun-shot wounds. It is based on that that if half of those persons received a single gun-shot injury, then the other half did not have a single gun-shot injury. Going through all the autopsy findings by Gordana Tomasevic, which we don't discuss, as you've said, I realise that there were many more gun-shot wounds on those bodies compared to what I stated. In any case, I referred to this example to illustrate the discrepancy between what is contained and what was the evidence found on the spot.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: So if I understand you correctly, you say based on the cartridge found on the spot then you can conclude that the number of persons killed is different than the number of persons alleged to have been killed. Would that be a fair summary of what you said -- what your position is?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Based on the number of cartridges found, it would seem that far fewer of the victims were killed in the locations where it is alleged that 150 people were killed.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: So you're just basing this conclusion on the absence of cartridges found on site by the team who conducted this --

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had this as material evidence and this is something I was able to address.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: From having reviewed this report that we have on the screen, the French mission report to Izbica, I presume that you are aware that they went to site in the summer of 1998 -- 1999, you know that, sir, around June of 1999 is when the French team went to Izbica?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what one can read in their report.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And you are aware, sir, I presume also from reading the report, that by the time the French team had arrived to the site of Izbica the bodies that had been buried there had, in fact, been exhumed by a mechanical digger and they were no longer there; you know that, sir, no?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And, in fact, sir, isn't it correct that you of all people are well familiar with the fact that this exhumation happened before the French team occurred because members of forensic teams from your institute, the VMA - and I'm speaking specifically of Mayor Miroslav Strbac and Dr. Gordana Tomasevic - they went to Kosovo at the time and Mayor Strbac he was there when the exhumations occurred, and this team later examined the bodies that were exhumed from Izbica, no? You know that, sir?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Now, sir, given that the bodies were removed from the site by a mechanical digger, it is -- you would accept the possibility, sir, that, in fact, the absence of cartridge cases on site could be simply the result of the exhumations that took place there before the French team arrived; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I understand you correctly, you say that during exhumation the cartridges went missing, the cartridges containing the projectiles which killed the victims. Is that your question?

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: What I'm saying, sir, is that the bodies were removed from the site, I mean a team from your medical institute went there along with other persons. They removed the bodies from the site. So the fact that cart -- there are not enough cartridges there or there are insufficient number of cartridges doesn't really tell us anything about how many persons were killed there, does it, because this could just -- the absence of cartridges could just simply be the result of the fact that there were exhumations there and they could have been removed or who else knows what happened to them, no? It could just simply be the result of that, sir, no?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. If one looks at the footage, one arrives at a conclusion that the dead bodies from the location where they were found were taken to the place of burial by members of the KLA, that is to say Albanian citizens of Kosovo. The forensic medical team headed by Dr. Strbac and Dr. Tomasevic carried out examinations not at the location where the people were killed but at the location where they were buried. And the conclusion or the proposition you put does not arise.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Sir, I'm not suggesting that your medical team carried out examinations at the location. What I'm saying is, there was a group of persons, including members of this forensic team, on site before the French team arrived, and they carried out exhumations of all these bodies with a mechanic digger.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: It was a slip of the tongue, in line 25, page 33, it should have been exhumations.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Okay. I'm sorry, sir. I have just been told there was an interpretation problem. I'm going to rephrase my question. What I'm suggesting to you, sir, is that given that the soil there was removed, there was a group of persons who went there and removed these bodies from where they had originally been buried, the simple absence of cartridges on site does not tell us anything about the number of persons killed there because anything could have happened to those cartridges; correct? I mean, we don't have that information, sir, do we?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We don't have that information, but it is clearly stated in the report how many cartridges were found. And if this is what was found on the scene then I used that to base my conclusion on. As for anyone was tasked with collecting cartridges, that is something I don't know. I can only address the issue of material evidence found on the location. From the documentation in the case file, it is not clear or stated that there was any heavy machinery involved. In the footage and photographs I saw, there were no construction machines there, or it doesn't seem that there had been any construction work carried out there. That is why it is difficult for me to accept the proposition that those pieces of machinery contributed to the cartridges going missing.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: The report does state that they found signs of digging by a mechanic digger, and you yourself have told us that you are aware that these bodies were removed from site; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The traces of the digger exist at the location where the bodies were buried and not where they were found. In the location where the bodies were buried, there were no cartridges. They could not have been found because there was no shooting there, which may be concluded from certain statements. The exhumation was carried out in another location, not the same location where the bodies were found.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Sir, the only point I'm making is we don't have sufficient evidence to know what happened to these cartridges, do we?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is your conclusion then.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: So given that we don't know, we can't really draw any conclusions from the absence of the cartridge cases on site with regard to the number of persons killed, can we, sir?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: One can draw that conclusion because it is in the case file. If there is some other information indicating that the cartridges were removed, then that is something that needs to be verified by looking at all the documents.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Now, sir, just to move on from this point. With regard to this report you were shown page 16 of the English and page 22 of the B/C/S, the conclusions. And your comment was that you found these totally unacceptable and specifically you comment on the findings made regarding the clothing and the bullet wounds, and this is at transcript page 13451. I think we have the wrong pages again on the screen. It's page -- yes -- do you recall saying that, sir, that you found the conclusions made in this report unacceptable and you specifically commented on the findings made in this report with regard to the bullet-holes in the clothing?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I also explained that between the time of burial and the time when the clothes were found there was a certain period of time which elapsed and that it is because of that that there was damage to the clothing. Those clothing items were also mixed with soil, and it is for all those reasons that I do not support the conclusion of the French forensic team.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: The report contains a detailed description of each item of clothing found, no, and were relevant also the number and diameter of bullet-holes that those who examined the clothing observed; correct? Maybe you can look at one of these while you're answering my question. Correct, sir, that the report contains a detailed description of each item of clothing and the bullet-holes and calibre of the weapon of -- based on the observations made of the clothing?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will read out the description at page 7. It is IS -- it's not that it's not only incorrect. ISD1, male jacket with a hood with two bullets in the upper third of the back, 60 centimetres from the bottom edge of the jacket corresponding to the entry wounds caused by gun-shots --

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- indicating that there was a point-blank range used. There is no description of the condition of the clothes or anything else. That is at page 7.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Sir, you would agree with me that the persons who found these items of clothing were able to observe bullet wounds, bullet-holes, in the clothing? That is something that's in the report, that's what they observed?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree with that, but if those persons observed that type of damage then as forensic medical experts they have to describe the diameter, the appearance, and any stains which may have come about because there was blood if there were any gun-shot wounds registered. The description as it stands serves no purpose. This is what I kept repeating before this Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: I see it's time for the break, Your Honours, but I can continue on this point after the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: If that's convenient, then we'll have the break now, and we resume in half an hour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Kravetz.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Sir, right before the break we were talking about the French forensic report, which we have up on the screen, and if we could go to page 4 in the English and page 5 in the B/C/S. And I was asking you about their conclusions regarding bullet-holes in the clothing, and you said if those persons observed that type of damage then as forensic medical experts they have to describe the diameter, the appearance, and any stains which they may have come about because -- if there was blood -- because if there was blood if there are any gun-shot wounds registered is what you said. Now, I want to draw your attention to case IS CI E1 which is at the bottom of the page in the B/C/S and also in English. And the comments made regarding this case, it says: "Adult man's wine-coloured lined jacket, size 54, with seven bullet-holes, three right dorsal, medial, and paramedial holes of which two are 8 millimetres in diameter and 30 centimetres from the bottom of the jacket; and another impact 8 millimetres in diameter plus three right lateral dorsal impacts 45 centimetres from the bottom of the jacket; and another right front impact 50 centimetres from the bottom of the jacket." Now, sir, isn't this French forensic team doing what you said that a forensic team should do had they observed bullet-holes on clothing that was recovered from site? They're providing a description of what is observed on the clothing.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there is something that is not good here. If the edges of the fabric are burned here, are they jagged edge or straight edge. Are there any foreign materials close to it or not. Is it dirty or not. So these are failings that I am permanently pointing out in my report. Yes, they are referred to, but there is no detailed description on matters that a conclusion would need to be made on.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: So you're saying that the information there about the diameter of each one of the bullet-holes, the number of holes, the location of the holes, the description of the clothing, that is not sufficient information in your view?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Why? You know when a projectile passes through fabric, that projectile that passes through would result in the fibres of the material pointing in the direction of the movement of the projectile. So, for example, this 8-millimetre hole then he could say the edge of the fabric is straight or jagged, the fibres of the fabric are facing inwards or outwards. And in that way the -- this would indicate the direction of the movement of the projectile --

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- we don't have that here. So on the basis of what can I then --

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: -- but isn't this simply just a description of what they found? This is what they saw, this is a description of what they found? Isn't that what this information is, sir?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Some people describe in more detail what they see. It depends on the person giving the description as to what they know is important and how much they convey what is important and put it on paper. I am just saying what else would need to be included about the defects in the fabric that I was describing in this case.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Very well, sir. And we have your position on that. Now, I want to direct your attention to paragraph 5. This is again relating to the Izbica site, and it's a paragraph where you comment on the video that you watched. And I understood you yesterday to say that you have actually watched the video footage that is referred to in paragraph 5 on a number of occasions in order to prepare your report and also to prepare yourself for testimony; is that correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And you told us yesterday that based on your viewing of this video footage you had arrived to the conclusion that bodies were found at at least nine locations, no, and I believe this is at 13452 of yesterday's transcript. Do you recall saying that yesterday, sir?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and I also mentioned the locations and the time counter on the footage where you can see that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: You are aware, sir, based on the information you were provided, witness statements and other materials regarding this site, that this video was not filmed for forensic purposes. It was filmed by villagers who arrived to the site after these killings had occurred? You are aware of that, sir?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that the footage was recorded by a doctor, Dr. Loshi or something, and I expected that a doctor would know what the crucial details would be to record the injuries on a body.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: The footage that was provided to this Tribunal by Dr. Loshi, but a different person, his name is Sefedin Thaqi is the one who actually filmed the bodies, and he is not a doctor. Do you know that sir, were you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I wasn't aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Now, the first portion that you referred to is at minute 1.15 from the start of the film, and you say: "It follows from the footage that one body wrapped up in a blanket was found in a quartermaster supply depot." Now, sir, Dr. Loshi testified here, and he explained that the initial portion of this video footage, in fact, has nothing to do with the Izbica site and that the footage concerning the Izbica site in fact starts much later, close to minute 7 of the footage, and this is at transcript page 740 and also P291, page 1. Were you -- did you have that information? Did you know that, sir, that the initial six minutes or so of the footage actually are showing something that's completely unrelated to the Izbica massacre site?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't know that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And now that you know that, sir, would that change your conclusion or your opinion that this is, in fact, evidence that the bodies -- that what is shown in this footage is evidence that bodies were found at different location, what you say here quartermaster supply depot. Now that you have this information would you change that conclusion?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If it is the way you say it is my findings would definitely be different, and I would say that the bodies were brought, instead of from nine locations were brought from eight locations.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Now, you -- the next video footage you referred to is the bodies lined up on a green meadow and you say: "They were brought there from elsewhere since the soles of their footwear show layers of mud while the metal surface is clean." I want to play this footage for you just very briefly, it's just like a second.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: If we could just have that displayed, and if it could be displayed for the witness as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: If we could play that briefly. And stop there.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Now, sir, this is the meadow and the persons with mud on their -- in their shoes that you were referring to in your report at minute 6.26 from the start of the film, correct? Is this what you're speaking about, bodies lined up in a green meadow?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Now, sir, isn't it correct that the fact that these bodies had mud on their shoes doesn't tell us -- that tells us nothing, in fact, of whether they were killed in this meadow or not because another explanation to the fact that they had mud on their shoes would be, for example, that they were marched through mud before reaching this site where the bodies were found. Isn't that another possible explanation?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's a possible explanation, but then the place where the bodies were found, does that -- are there fired shells, spent shells there? Have any spent shells been found in that place where the bodies are found?

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: But you're now bringing a completely different element here in the equation talking about spent shells. I mean, your conclusion was simply based on the mud on their shoes, and what I'm putting to you is the fact that what the portion of the video we saw there which shows bodies lying on a meadow with muddy shoes, that doesn't tell us anything of whether the bodies were brought from elsewhere or not, doesn't it, sir, the mud on the shoes?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The mud on the shoes would tell us that they walked through mud; that is quite clear. Now, if they were walking on the meadow and in view of the size of the meadow, the thick layer of mud on the soles of their shoes would not be so thick. It wouldn't be there because if you walk on the grassy surface of the meadow, the -- most of the mud would have been removed, most of it.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: But, sir, you have no information of where these persons were made to walk through before they ended up in this meadow. You don't know that, do you, sir?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have to know that while working on the expertise. I don't have to know many of the details that I am writing a report on. I reach many of the conclusions on the basis of the information that I glean from the data that is made available to me. I don't have any prior information before I embark on my expertise.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Yes, I understand that. But you said if they were walking on the meadow and in view of the size of the meadow, the thick layer of mud on the soles of their shoes would not be so thick, but you do not know if that's the case, sir, do you? You don't know if these persons were walking on the meadow before they reached this site and were executed?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is exactly what I'm talking about. I'm saying that they were brought there, not that they walked on the meadow. Had they walked on the meadow the layer of mud would not have been so thick. Had they been brought there while they were still alive, I don't know -- I assume that they were brought there after their death.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: But they could have also been brought there and walked through mud while they were still alive, and that would explain the mud on the soles of the shoes, no? That is another explanation, no?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did agree with you, but I said that after being walked through mud and which we cannot see in this footage, there is the meadow and 10 or more metres of walking on the grass-covered surface would lead to the mud being removed from the soles of the footwear. And then you would end up with a much thinner layer of mud on the bottoms of the footwear that were in contact with the grassy surface of the meadow.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: But you're saying that on the basis of your assumption that the meadow looked like this, like we saw it on the footage, the day these persons were killed? You're assuming that this is what the meadow looked like at the time?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The bodies were found. The bodies looked fresh. On the basis of the footage, you can see that these are fresh bodies. They're not putrefying, decomposing bodies. I didn't look at the details, and I did not look at it in detail in terms of this particular question, but the bodies seem to be fresh and the time of death seems to have occurred a couple of days earlier. That is why the surface of the meadow could not have changed in that period. We can see that it's covered with grass and that would indicate that this condition of the meadow lasted for some period of time which was longer than the time since the death of these people on -- whose bodies are on the meadow.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Sir, the evidence we've heard here from persons who were at Izbica on the days preceding the killings of these persons was that it was raining heavily, in fact. For all we know, sir, the meadow and all areas around there could have been quite muddy at the time, no? There could have been mud everywhere including the place where these persons walked through? That is possible, sir, no?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's possible, but you cannot see that on this video footage. You cannot make such a conclusion on the basis of what is seen in the video footage.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: So you would agree with me, sir, we can't make a conclusion either way? We can't make a conclusion that these bodies were brought from elsewhere, we can also not make the conclusion that they walked through -- we don't know, actually, we can't make a conclusion either way based -- just solely based on this footage?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am prepared to defend my findings, and I remain by what I say that are my findings.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Very well, sir. Now, another comment you make is -- and that's just a couple of lines further down is that: "Traces of blood that ran from the nose and the mouth and the wounds are in a different direction from the position of the body." Are you suggesting here, sir, by saying this, that this is an indication that the bodies were brought from elsewhere, the fact that traces of blood ran from the nose and mouth and the wounds in a different direction from the position of the body?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STANKOVIC [Resumed]
